segments.narration: 120 feet beneath Lake Huron sits an ancient stone wall. Sonar mapped parallel lines of stacked boulders stretching across the dark lakebed.
These were no natural rock piles. They formed clear drive lanes complete with circular stone blinds tucked along the sides.
segments.visual_query: underwater lake huron stone wall boulders

segments.narration: Who could build a complex hunting trap deep underwater? The massive structure made no sense in modern geography.
segments.visual_query: great lakes deep water dark blue

segments.narration: In 2014, archaeologists uncovered the truth. Nine thousand years ago, ice age water levels were two hundred feet lower, leaving dry land.
Paleo-Indian hunters built the walls to trap migrating caribou herds, right before melting glaciers flooded the entire canyon.
